title: Live-Cell Imaging of Mitochondrial Redox State in Yeast Cells
protocol: Transfer 1 mL of mid-log culture grown in SC liquid medium to a 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add DHE to the cell suspension to achieve a final concentration of 40 μM (4 μL of a 10 mM stock is added to 1,000 μL of cell suspension).
Return the remaining cells in the 50 mL conical tube to the incubator and propagate at 30°C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Incubate the cells with DHE for 30 min at 30°C in the dark.
Concentrate cells by centrifugation at 6,000 × g for 30 s, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL SC.
Repeat step of concentrating cells once more.
Centrifuge the cells again at 6,000 × g for 30 s, remove most of the supernatant but leave 10–20 μL to keep the cells moist.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the residual medium.
Transfer 1.7 μL of the resuspended cell suspension to a microscope slide.
Cover the sample on the slide with a coverslip.
Image each slide for no more than 10 minutes.
If additional slides are needed, prepare them using the remaining culture and repeat the previous steps.
Acquire a z-series image using GFPEnvy filter settings: excitation/emission 470/507 nm, 20% power, typical exposure time of 200 ms.
Acquire a z-series image using DHE filter settings: excitation/emission 550/610 nm, 80% power, typical exposure time of 300 ms.
Use 1 × 1 binning for optimal pixel dimension less than 0.1 μm.
Capture 21 z sections with a spacing of 0.3 μm to cover a total depth of 6 μm.
Acquire GFPEnvy z-stacks.
Acquire DHE z-stacks.
Enter pixel size in X, Y, and Z as 0.0645, 0.0645, and 0.3 μm respectively.
Go to Actions→ Create New→ Calculated PSF (Point Spread Function).
Set up PSF parameters by entering microscope type, immersion medium refractive index, objective lens numerical aperture, and emission wavelength.
Use wide-field, 1.52, 1.4, and 507 nm for GFPEnvy.
Use 610 nm for DHE.
Go to Tools→ Iterative Restoration.
Use 60 iterations and a 100% confidence criterion for termination.
Start the deconvolution.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) in an area without cells.
Export data including mean intensity from the Measurement tab to a spreadsheet for analysis as mean background intensity.
Draw an outline of a cell using a freehand ROI tool.
Create a protocol in the Measurement tab to obtain mitochondrial DHE.
Find objects by thresholding the intensity of GFPEnvy signals to identify mitochondria.
Clip these mitochondrial objects to ROIs representing outlines of mitochondria.
Measure mean intensity in the DHE channel for these clipped objects.
Calculate mitochondrial superoxide levels as the mean DHE intensity in mitochondria minus background intensity.
Set up thresholds from an ROI drawn in an area where there are no cells.
Select Channel X and Channel Y as the DHE channel and GFPEnvy channel, respectively.
Draw an outline of a cell using a freehand ROI tool.
Download the Diffraction PSF 3D plugin from the Fiji website.
Install the Iterative Deconvolve 3D plugin from the Fiji website.
Create a PSF using Plugins → Diffraction PSF 3D.
Enter immersion medium refractive index, objective lens numerical aperture, emission wavelength, image pixel size, image z step size, image width, image height, and image Z stack in PSF parameters.
Open deconvolved images in Fiji using the Bio-Formats importer: Plugins → Bio-Formats Importer.
Select “split channels.”
Keep the brightfield channel, deconvolved DHE channel and GFPEnvy channel open.
Close unused channels.
Import images for analysis.
Subtract background intensity in the DHE channel using Fiji software.
Generate a maximum projection of the DHE channel: Image → Stacks → Z project.
Set start and stop slices to include all relevant sections.
Select “Average Intensity” as the projection type.
Go to Analyze → Set measurements, and check “Mean gray value.”
Use the Rectangle selection tool to select a background region without cells.
Measure mean intensity in the selected background region.
Subtract the mean background intensity from the image using Process → Math → Subtract.
Enter the previously measured mean background intensity for subtraction.
Process all slices after subtracting background intensity.
Adjust the provided value if necessary to remove most of the background.
If background intensity remains visible, use rolling ball background subtraction as an alternative method.
Outline a cell in the brightfield channel using the freehand selection tool.
Add the outlined cell to the ROI Manager.
Use ROI Manager to recall the ROI on both GFPEnvy and DHE channels.
Duplicate the cell image in ROI: Image → Duplicate.
Remove the cell outline ROI once duplication is done.
Threshold the GFPEnvy channel to create masks of mitochondria.
Select the GFPEnvy channel, Image → Adjust → Threshold.
Adjust the threshold to segment mitochondria in the GFPEnvy channel and click Apply.
Uncheck “calculate threshold for each image” and check “Black background (of binary masks)” when prompted.
Apply the settings to all slices in the stack.
Add all the masks to the ROI Manager: Select the stack containing the binary masks of mitochondria.
Analyze → Analyze Particles, keep Size and Circularity to default values to include all mitochondria.
Select “Add to Manager” and “Exclude on edges.”
Process all slices in the stack.
Go to Analyze → Set measurements, check “Area” and “Integrated density.”
Clear the results before proceeding to the next step.
Measure the DHE signal using the mitochondria mask in ROI Manager: Select the window containing the DHE channel.
Go to ROI Manager and click Measure.
Export data to a spreadsheet for analysis.
Sum the area and integrated density (IntDen) in one cell.
Divide the summed integrated density by summed area to obtain the superoxide level in the mitochondria.
Go to Analyze → Set measurements and check “Mean gray value.”
Select a background region where there are no cells using the Rectangle selection tool.
Measure the mean intensity in the selected background region.
Subtract the mean background mean intensity from all slices: Process → Math → Subtract.
Enter the mean background intensity measured previously.
Process all slices to subtract the background intensity.
Outline a cell in the brightfield channel using the freehand selection tool.
Add the outlined cell to the ROI Manager.
Perform Coloc2 analysis: Analyze → Colocalization → Coloc2.
Select channel 1 and channel 2 as DHE and GFPEnvy channels, respectively.
For ROI or mask setting, select “ROI Manager” to import the ROI selected previously.
Use Bisection as threshold regression method.
Select “Manders’ Correlation” under Algorithms.
Transfer 1 mL of mid-log culture in SC to each of three 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add H2O2 to one culture to a final concentration of 5 mM.
Incubate the cultures with H2O2 at 30°C for 30 minutes.
Add DTT to another culture to a final concentration of 5 mM.
Incubate the cultures with DTT at 30°C for 30 minutes.
Return remaining cells in the 50 mL conical tube to the incubator and propagate at 30°C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Concentrate cells by centrifugation at 6,000 × g for 30 seconds.
Remove supernatant from the tubes, leaving 10–20 μL of supernatant in each tube.
Resuspend the pellet in the residual medium.
Transfer 1.7 μL of cell suspension to a microscope slide.
Cover the cell suspension with a coverslip.
Resuspend cells in the appropriate volume of supernatant for imaging.
Acquire a z-series by locating a field of cells.
Set excitation/emission 365/500–550 nm for oxidized mito-roGFP: use 50% power and typical exposure time of 300 ms.
Set excitation/emission 470/500–550 nm for reduced mito-roGFP: use 20% power and typical exposure time of 200 ms.
Use 1 × 1 binning (if camera chip has sufficient pixels, 2 × 2 binning may be used; final pixel dimension should be <0.1 μm).
Acquire 21 z sections with 0.3 μm spacing.
Set software to excite at 365 and 470 nm sequentially at each z step.
Acquire 5–6 images per slide, and 2–3 slides per sample to obtain images of approximately 100 cells.
Deconvolve images using Volocity or Fiji software.
Import images into a Volocity library and create an image sequence with two channels.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) in an area where there are no cells.
Choose Tools → Ratio.
Calculate the background: Get From ROI.
Adjust the threshold to include mitochondrial structures.
Check the option to apply a rainbow LUT to the ratio channel.
Select the Measurement tab and select the ratio channel.
Draw an ROI around the area of interest.
Measure the ratio channel, excluding zero values.
Export data to a spreadsheet for analysis.
Convert images to TIFF format.
Verify pixel values using the histogram in Fiji.
Open images and change type to 32 bit: Image→ Type → 32 bit.
Draw a region of interest (ROI) in an area where there are no cells.
Calculate the mean intensity in this ROI: Analyze → Measure.
Subtract the calculated mean background from the stack: Process → Math → Subtract.
Find the middle slice and threshold on mitochondria: Image → Adjust → Threshold.
Apply the threshold to all slices in the stack.
Create the ratio z stack using Fiji: Process → Image Calculator.
Divide the reduced (470 nm excitation) stack by the oxidized (365 nm excitation) stack.
Draw an ROI around the area of interest in Fiji.
Choose Analyze → Tools → ROI Manager and click Add to store the ROI.
Select all ROIs in ROI Manager, then choose More → Multi-Measure to measure all stack slices.
Export data to a spreadsheet for analysis.
Multiply the mean intensity and area to obtain integrated intensity in the spreadsheet.
Divide the summed integrated intensity by summed area to obtain the mean ratio in the mitochondria.
